title: ‘Ginny & Georgia’ Season 4 First Look: The Past Is Never Far Behind (Exclusive)
text:

 Plus, we can exclusively share the season 4 release date. By P. Claire Dodson November 18, 2026 Courtesy of Netflix In Ginny & Georgia season 4, the trauma of the past is never far behind for our conflicted mother-daughter heroines—and for the idyllic fictional Massachusetts town of Wellsbury.
 Teen Vogue can exclusively announce that the Ginny & Georgia season 4 release date is January 21, 2027. That means it’s only a few short months until the Miller family and their classmates and neighbors return to our screens, and it’s safe to say that things are different now after the turbulent events of season 3 .
 Last season saw Georgia (Brianne Howey) escape a prison sentence by the skin of her teeth thanks to some help from Ginny ( Antonia Gentry ), who has realized she might be more like her mother than she hoped. Austin ( Diesel La Torraca ), who has a more intense role in season 4, witnessed his mom murder his best friend’s dad and then watched as his own dad was framed for that murder, so that’s going to leave a mark.
 Meanwhile, Ginny’s neighbor and love interest Marcus Baker ( Felix Mallard ) is headed for in-patient treatment for alcoholism and depression, and Ginny’s former best friend Maxine ( Sara Waisglass ) doesn’t seem to be doing too well either in the aftermath of their argument. MANG—the friend group of Ginny, Max, Abby (Katie Douglas), and Norah (Chelsea Clark)—is hanging by a thread. To escape it all, Ginny heads for a much-needed summer vacation with her dad in South Korea.
 “The plan was always that season 3 was about the bomb going off, and season 4 is really about what happens when the dust settles and every character is slightly altered by the events of last season,” creator, co-showrunner, and executive producer Sarah Lampert tells Teen Vogue . “Season 3, while it was really emotional, it really had a lot of plot. Season 4 is more character-driven, and it is kind of sinking back into this more character place of emotions and relationships. The question of what happens after, how to move forward.”
 Adds co-showrunner and executive producer Sarah Glinski, “Can you have a fresh start? Is that really possible? Can you move forward? We all carry all our past with us all the time.”
 Season 4 picks up as Ginny returns for her junior year, with a new hairstyle and, potentially, a new outlook on life. “In the beginning, I was like, ‘I don't know this version of Ginny.’ Like, ‘Who is this girl?’ Gentry laughs.
 Netflix “Ginny is in her, I like to say, healing era,” she adds. ”She's coming back into her junior year a better, more realized version of herself, which I appreciate because this girl has been through so much. It was nice to see her really, really focused on keeping her head down, trying to stay mentally healthy and focused, and not trying to be pulled so much into all the drama that constantly occurs in her life. This is a version of Ginny that I liked seeing when I watched the season back, because it's a more mature version of her where there's a little bit less angst.”
 Still, drama always seems to creep its way in where Ginny and Georgia are involved. Georgia, for her part, is dealing with the emotional ramifications of an extremely public court case, in addition to navigating fraught relationships with her exes. Oh, and she’s pregnant and doesn’t know who the father is, and Ginny is the only one who knows her secret.
 “As always, the stakes are so high,” Howey says. “I think Georgia's MO season four is to prove that she's a good mom. She just wants to prove to Ginny and Austin that she can be a good mom to them, and a new mom to them, without continuing these horrible cycles that she inherited, this generational trauma that she inherited.”
 Let’s just say Georgia faces a fair amount of challenges in setting out to prove that.
 “She doesn't have any money, she needs a job, she's pregnant, she doesn't know who the father is. Ginny's been gone all summer, which is the worst feeling in the world for Georgia. She's very codependent on her. And Austin is going through puberty, his hormones are raging, and wants nothing to do with Georgia,” says Howey. “So, I think when we see Georgia at the top of season four, she's pretty lost and just trying to fake it until she makes it. She's been in hiding all summer. For a woman who always has the next step set up, Georgia doesn't have the next step set up this time.”
 Netflix Netflix Netflix The character of Austin gets a fresh amount of depth in the show’s fourth season. (He’s also taller. “He's the size of a building now,” jokes Gentry.) Lampert says they “lucked out” with La Torraca. “We hired Diesel and we had no idea how he was going to grow,” she says. “And he's fantastic. He is so talented. He makes it exciting to write for him, and he just tackles everything. So he has a bigger role in Season 4 than he has before, and I think that we were excited he was tackling this character in such a great way.
 “Obviously the title of the show is Ginny & Georgia ,” she adds. “And one of my favorite tweets from Season 1 was, ‘Doesn't she have another kid? What about Austin?’ I always thought that was so funny, but it's true. What about Austin? Honestly, it's a big theme of the show, what about Austin? There's this idea that he's this kid who really is slipping through the cracks … So many people are trying to alert Georgia to the fact that Austin might need extra support. And Georgia has really, up until this point, really studiously ignored that and denied it, because she doesn't want any weakness attributed to anyone in her family because she thinks that makes them a target, because that's what it was like for her growing up.”
 Howey laughs when she thinks of Austin and Georgia’s dynamic this season: “I was like, ‘God, parenthood is hard. It's just one kid after another. Is this what my future holds?’”
 Netflix Netflix Then there’s the Max of it all. Season 3 episode 9 was centered around her perspective, where we got a real in-depth look at how her personality is shaped by her upbringing, and how perpetually being thought of as either “the girl who is always OK” or “the girl who is always doing way too much” has diminished her as a person.
 “Max ended, obviously, in a pretty dark place at the end of season 3. But also, I think in a really relatable place for most young people, which is a breakup with all your friends,” Glinski says. Expect more of that journey in season 4. “We basically wanted to start where we ended, because it's such an important story to tell. We really catch up with Max pretty close to where we left her, except a couple of months have passed.”
 Netflix Lampert, who based much of Max on herself, says it’s been gratifying to see the ways audiences have related to Max’s struggles. “The really beautiful thing about Max's storyline, to me, is it just feels really authentic to the fact that she doesn't understand what's going on around her, but her feelings are really big and really valid,” Lampert says. “She's dealing with undiagnosed mental health [struggles], and at the same time, really struggling with the fact that she feels like she's losing her brother, she feels like she's losing her friends. And I think most importantly, she feels like she's losing her sense of self, and that's how we kind of leave Season 3 with her.
 “So entering Season 4, I think it's really about watching Max, and seeing how does this character who feels that she's only succeeding at her job when she's being so big and bright and bold and fixing everyone else around her, and is offering so much to all of her relationships, [cope] when those relationships reject her … We've all gone through feelings of feeling left out, of feeling like, ‘What if my friends don't like me anymore? What have I done wrong? Am I a bad person?’”
 But she hints at some sort of growth for Max this season, and for Marcus, and for their sibling relationship: “They've grown so far apart, and I think the question of the Baker Twins this season is, what's it going to take to get them back together?”
 Netflix Netflix On the Max and Ginny front, Gentry has been fascinated to see the conversations around their altercation at the house party in season 3.
 “I remember filming that and thinking to myself, ‘There's a way to have this conversation where Ginny doesn't have to be mean, but I felt like the creators, they were like, ‘No, no, she's in a completely different mental space right now. She needs to make it hurt.’ And she says it so flippantly, and I don't even think she realized how harsh it came off,” Gentry says. “I was thinking back about high school relationships, especially with female friendships, it's all so complicated.
 “For Maxine, her friends, that's her entire world. For Ginny, her entire world all of season three was, ‘My mom killed someone and I need to get her out.’ So, I don't think she was really thinking about how she was hurting Max. She didn't have room to think about that. But I do think in season four, we see a new side of their friendship and then MANG as a whole, there's just always evolving emotions and I don't know, just the versions of themselves that sometimes fit together, sometimes don't.”
 Netflix Netflix While the cast and showrunners can’t say too much about specific plot details to come this season, they do say to keep an eye out for episodes 1 and 7, and the school musical this time around. Plus, stay tuned for some unexpected pairings and new information about the characters fans know so well, says Glinski. And no matter how the past comes back to haunt Ginny and Georgia, expect the show’s vulnerable emotional core to continue.
 “We want the show to be fun and entertaining and all of that, but to me, the show has always been a story about mental health disguised as a fun mother-daughter murder show,” Lampert says. “Because the core of it really is about these characters and their relationships.”
